questions.question: Which tracking technology is included in the others category of tracking technologies used in VR and AR?
options: Inertial tracking
Hybrid tracking
Vision-based tracking
Electromechanical tracking
questions.explanation: The main categories are electromechanical, electromagnetic, acoustic or ultrasonic, vision-based, inertial, and others; the others category includes location-based and hybrid tracking.

questions.question: What is the main structural feature of electromechanical trackers?
options: Optical sensors that detect targets emitting or reflecting light.
A serial or parallel kinematic structure of interconnected links with joint sensors.
A stationary transmitter that creates a magnetic field measured by a receiver.
Ultrasonic signals exchanged between stationary speakers and a headset microphone.
questions.explanation: Electromechanical trackers consist of a serial or parallel kinematic structure made of links connected by joints with sensors.

questions.question: What are the two types of electromechanical trackers?
options: Inside-out trackers and outside-in trackers
Magnetic trackers and acoustic trackers
Transmitter trackers and receiver trackers
World-fixed trackers and wearable trackers.
questions.explanation: Electromechanical trackers are of two types: world-fixed trackers and wearable trackers.

questions.question: What characterizes a world-fixed electromechanical tracker?
options: A cumbersome setup with a display, mechanical pivoting, tracking sensors, and a counterbalance for stability.
A device worn on the body that translates the wearer's movement into avatar movement.
A non-contact system in which a receiver moves with the head inside a magnetic field.
A system that uses stationary ultrasonic transmitters and microphones to track a head-mounted display.
questions.explanation: A world-fixed electromechanical tracker is described as a cumbersome setup with a display, mechanical pivoting, tracking sensors, and a counterbalance.

questions.question: What is the function of a wearable electromechanical tracker?
options: It provides a stable display mounted on a mechanically pivoting tracked setup.
It is worn on a person's body and translates that person's movements into animated avatar movement.
It determines pose using infrared targets that emit or reflect light.
It obtains a headset position from the direction of a magnetic field.
questions.explanation: Wearable electromechanical trackers are worn on a person's body and track and translate that person's movements into animated avatar movement.

questions.question: Why are wearable electromechanical trackers used only in limited, highly specialized setups?
options: They are not very comfortable to wear and are quite cumbersome.
They are very comfortable to wear and are widely used in consumer applications.
They rely on visible-light sensors that are affected by poor ambient lighting.
They require a clear line of sight between transmitters and receivers.
questions.explanation: Wearable electromechanical trackers are not very comfortable to wear, are quite cumbersome, and are used in limited, highly specialized setups.

questions.question: How does an electromagnetic tracker obtain the real-time position of the receiver?
options: From the arrival time of ultrasonic pulses at the receiver
From infrared light reflected by targets in the room
From the angles of serial or parallel mechanical joints
From the direction of the magnetic field produced by a stationary transmitter
questions.explanation: An electromagnetic tracker uses a stationary transmitter to produce a magnetic field, and the receiver's position is obtained from the magnetic field direction.

questions.question: In an electromagnetic tracker, what do the transmitter's magnetic fields help generate in the receiver?
options: Ultrasonic pressure waves in a microphone
Alternating current or direct current signals
Infrared pulses for an optical camera
Mechanical motion in a kinematic arm
questions.explanation: The transmitter's magnetic fields generate alternating current or direct current in the receiver, and these currents help track the head's position.

questions.question: What signals are used by an acoustic tracker to determine the position of a head-mounted display?
options: Ultrasonic signals from stationary transmitters
Visible light from optical cameras
Joint angle readings from wearable sensors
Magnetic field directions from stationary transmitters
questions.explanation: Acoustic or ultrasonic tracking uses ultrasonic signals from stationary transmitters to determine the real-time position of receivers attached to an HMD.

questions.question: Which setup is common to electromagnetic and acoustic tracking?
options: Fixed transmitters and fixed receivers
Stationary transmitters and receivers that move with the head or body
Cameras fixed to the room and markers on the headset
Movable transmitters and receivers fixed to the room
questions.explanation: Both electromagnetic and acoustic tracking use stationary transmitters and receivers that move with the head or the user's body.

questions.question: Which statement correctly compares the line-of-sight requirement of acoustic and electromagnetic tracking?
options: Electromagnetic tracking requires an unobstructed line of sight, whereas acoustic tracking does not
Acoustic tracking requires an unobstructed line of sight, whereas electromagnetic tracking does not
Both require an unobstructed line of sight
Neither requires an unobstructed line of sight
questions.explanation: Acoustic or ultrasonic tracking requires line of sight between transmitter and receiver with no obstacle in between, while electromagnetic tracking does not require this line of sight.

questions.question: What do vision-based trackers use to determine an object's pose?
options: Optical sensors or cameras
Electromechanical kinematic joints
Magnetic fields from a transmitter
Ultrasonic signals from speakers
questions.explanation: Vision-based trackers determine poses, such as position and orientation, using optical sensors or cameras.

questions.question: What are the three main categories of optical sensors used to detect or track a pose?
options: Fiducial, natural feature, and model-based techniques
Transmitters, receivers, and kinematic joints
Infrared, ultrasonic, and electromagnetic sensors
Infrared, visible light, and 3D structure sensors
questions.explanation: The three main categories of optical sensors for pose detection or tracking are infrared sensors, visible light sensors, and 3D structure sensors.

questions.question: Why is infrared tracking less affected by poor ambient lighting or harsh shadows?
options: It uses visible light cameras with high dynamic range
It relies on infrared sensing rather than visible light sensing
It increases the brightness of visible-light targets
It removes obstacles between transmitter and receiver
questions.explanation: Infrared tracking is robust to adverse illumination effects because it relies on infrared sensing rather than visible light sensing.

questions.question: In outside-looking-in infrared tracking, where are the cameras placed?
options: Mounted with the user to detect external targets
On the tracked object, facing outward
Fixed to a transmitter that produces a magnetic field
In the environment, not on the tracked object
questions.explanation: In outside looking in infrared tracking, cameras placed in the environment detect targets attached to the tracked object.

questions.question: In inside-looking-out infrared tracking, how does the camera obtain pose information?
options: It measures magnetic fields produced by three antennas
It is mounted with the user and detects external targets
It is placed in the environment and detects targets attached to the object
It emits ultrasonic signals that reflect from a fixed transmitter
questions.explanation: In inside looking out infrared tracking, the camera is mounted with the user and estimates poses from external targets.

questions.question: Which sensors are used for visible light tracking?
options: Visible light sensors or 3D structure sensors
Visible light sensors or optical cameras
Infrared sensors or optical cameras
Infrared sensors or 3D structure sensors
questions.explanation: Visible light tracking uses visible light sensors or optical cameras, and optical cameras are widely available in consumer and wearable devices.

questions.question: Which three techniques are classified under visible light tracking?
options: Fiducial tracking, natural feature tracking, and model-based tracking
Infrared tracking, visible light tracking, and model-based tracking
Fiducial tracking, natural feature tracking, and infrared tracking
Outside-looking-in tracking, inside-looking-out tracking, and model-based tracking
questions.explanation: Visible light tracking is classified into fiducial tracking, natural feature tracking, and model-based tracking.

questions.question: What does fiducial tracking add to the environment to aid registration and tracking?
options: Existing environmental features such as points and corners
Artificial landmarks called fiducials
Virtual alignment between real and digital content
Infrared targets that emit or reflect light
questions.explanation: Fiducial tracking adds fiducials, which are artificial landmarks in the environment, to aid registration and tracking of the object being tracked.

questions.question: Which fiducial type is used for detection at greater distances?
options: Small colored LEDs or pieces of paper
Proportional width ring fiducials
Multi-ring fiducials
Constant width ring fiducials
questions.explanation: Among the listed fiducial kinds, multi-ring fiducials are used for detection at greater distances.

questions.question: In natural feature tracking, what is registered in real time?
options: The camera pose
The virtual environment model
The user's hand gesture
The fiducial marker position
questions.explanation: Natural feature tracking registers camera pose in real time using features already present in the natural environment.

questions.question: Which items are given as examples of features detected in natural feature tracking?
options: Points, corners, and line intersections
Multi-ring fiducial markers
Virtual objects generated by the software
Small colored LEDs and pieces of paper
questions.explanation: The image processing algorithms detect features unique to the surroundings, such as points, corners, and line intersections.

questions.question: What role do unique feature descriptors serve in natural feature tracking?
options: They detect points, corners, and line intersections
They identify and differentiate one feature from other features.
They create the virtual environment to be rendered
They add artificial landmarks to the environment
questions.explanation: Unique descriptors are calculated for each detected feature so that one feature can be identified and differentiated from other features.

questions.question: How is the camera pose estimated in natural feature tracking?
options: By tracking the user's gestures
By comparing the camera image with a rendered virtual scene
By adding fiducial markers to the environment
By matching features in the scene with features in the object using their descriptors
questions.explanation: Camera pose is estimated by using the calculated feature descriptors to match features detected in the scene with features detected in the object to be tracked.

activities.title: Order the stages of natural feature tracking

items.title: Order the stages of natural feature tracking
steps: Environmental and object features are detected
Unique descriptors are computed for each feature
Scene features are matched with object features
Camera pose is estimated from matched features

questions.question: Which process is described by Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM)?
options: It uses artificial landmarks added to the environment to aid registration.
It matches scene feature descriptors with feature descriptors on a tracked object.
It creates and updates a map of a real environment while localizing positions within it.
It uses structured-light depth data to build 3D models of structures.
questions.explanation: SLAM simultaneously creates and updates a map of the real environment while localizing positions within it.

questions.question: Which tracking capability is attributed to SLAM?
options: Drift-free tracking of already mapped environments only
Feature matching between the scene and a tracked object
Pose estimation using artificial fiducials in the environment
Drift-free tracking of unknown environments
questions.explanation: SLAM allows drift-free tracking of unknown environments.

questions.question: How does Parallel Tracking and Mapping (PTAM) optimize SLAM?
options: It matches scene features to features on the tracked object for pose.
It tracks the camera and maps the environment as separate activities.
It tracks the camera and maps the environment as a single combined activity.
It adds artificial landmarks to the environment to guide camera tracking.
questions.explanation: PTAM is a further optimization of SLAM that allows tracking of the camera and mapping of the environment as separate activities.

questions.question: What improvement is associated with PTAM?
options: Improved tracking accuracy but not overall performance
Reduced computational requirements for larger environments
Improved tracking accuracy and overall performance
Improved overall performance but not tracking accuracy
questions.explanation: PTAM improved both the accuracy of tracking and the overall performance.

questions.question: Why is PTAM more suitable for smaller environments?
options: Its computational requirements for smaller environments are quite high
It cannot map the environment while tracking the camera
Its computational requirements for larger environments are quite high
It requires artificial fiducials to be placed in the environment
questions.explanation: PTAM is more suitable for smaller environments because the computational requirements for larger environments are quite high.

questions.question: What does 3D structure tracking create from the 3D positions of points in the scene?
options: 2D maps of virtual environments
3D models of virtual avatars only
Inertial measurements of orientation change
3D models of structures in the environment
questions.explanation: 3D structure tracking uses commercial sensors to obtain 3D positions of points and creates 3D models of structures in the environment for augmenting the real-world view.

questions.question: What development made 3D structure sensing more accessible in recent years?
options: Inertial trackers began measuring absolute position values
PTAM became suitable for larger environments
SLAM stopped updating maps over time
Commercial sensors for 3D structure information became affordable
questions.explanation: Commercial sensors capable of detecting 3D structure information from the environment became affordable in recent years.

questions.question: What sensor data does Kinect Fusion use to create high-quality 3D models?
options: Data from a magnetic field sensor
Data from a gyroscope measuring rotation rate
Data from an inertial accelerometer
Data from the Kinect's structured light depth sensor
questions.explanation: Kinect Fusion uses data from the Kinect's structured light depth sensor to create high-quality 3D models of real objects and environments.

questions.question: What do inertial trackers measure?
options: Changes in orientation, translation velocity, or acceleration
Absolute orientations of objects
Absolute positions of objects
GPS signal carrier waves
questions.explanation: Inertial trackers measure rate of change in orientation, translation velocity, or acceleration rather than absolute values.

questions.question: Why can inertial trackers be readily used in devices such as smartphones and head-mounted displays?
options: They are typically built-in MEMS sensors with no range limitation
They rely on external GPS satellites
They require visible light cameras
They depend on acoustic markers
questions.explanation: Inertial trackers are typically based on MEMS, are part of the device the user is using, and have no range limitation.

questions.question: What can be created from a gyroscope, an accelerometer, and a magnetometer?
options: A basic light-based sensor
A hybrid software-level sensor
A 3D structure sensing system
An external electromagnetic tracker
questions.explanation: Hybrid software-level sensors can be designed using the primary inertial sensors: a gyroscope, an accelerometer, and a magnetometer.

questions.question: When is GPS generally appropriate for tracking?
options: When high-accuracy position registration is required
When absolute orientation must be obtained
When an approximate position is enough, outdoors, or in a hybrid tracking system
When precise indoor positioning is required
questions.explanation: GPS is useful outdoors but generally has low accuracy, especially indoors, and allows only positional tracking; it is typically used when an approximation is good enough or as part of a hybrid tracking system.

questions.question: How can RTK improve a basic GPS sensor?
options: By removing the need for a GPS sensor
By switching to inertial tracking only
By using GPS signal carrier waves to improve detection accuracy
By measuring absolute orientation
questions.explanation: RTK can be used with a basic GPS sensor to improve detection accuracy by using GPS signal carrier waves for measurement.

questions.question: What is motion capture?
options: A positional tracking device useful outdoors
A self-contained sensor that measures changes in orientation
Digitally recording movements of real things, usually humans
A fundamentally new basic tracking method
questions.explanation: Motion capture is a technique for digitally recording movements of real things, usually humans, and it can be based on any tracking method.

questions.question: What is true about motion capture with respect to real-time tracking?
options: It must be real-time tracking
It may be non-real-time tracking
It can only be done with real-time cameras
It is limited to real-time wearable suits
questions.explanation: Motion capture need not be real-time tracking; it can be non-real-time tracking as well.

questions.question: What do eye-tracking systems typically track?
options: The 3D positions of points in the environment
The rate of change in head orientation
The position of a user in outdoor environments
The gaze point or area of the user's gaze
questions.explanation: Eye-tracking systems typically track the gaze point or area of the gaze of the user.

questions.question: What defines a hybrid tracker?
options: A tracker that uses an inertial sensor only
A tracker that uses a GPS sensor only
A tracker that uses a 3D structure sensor only
A tracker that combines two or more basic tracking approaches
questions.explanation: A hybrid tracker uses two or more basic tracking systems or approaches, formed by combining basic tracking methods.

questions.question: How do hybrid trackers typically perform compared with single-technology tracking?
options: They perform better
They perform the same
They perform only outdoors
They perform worse
questions.explanation: Hybrid trackers have typically been found to perform better than single-technology-based tracking.

questions.question: How are electromagnetic tracking and acoustic tracking similar in their sensor placement, and what practical difference matters when obstacles may be present?
questions.reference_answer: Both use a stationary transmitter in the environment and a receiver that moves with the head-mounted display. In electromagnetic tracking, position is obtained from the magnetic field direction and the system does not require line of sight. Acoustic or ultrasonic tracking uses ultrasonic signals and requires an unobstructed line of sight between transmitter and receiver.

questions.question: How can a hybrid tracking system improve on the limitation of an inertial tracker found in many head-mounted displays?
questions.reference_answer: Inertial trackers measure changes in orientation, translation velocity, or acceleration rather than absolute values. They are typically MEMS-based and can be part of a head-mounted display. A hybrid tracker combines two or more basic tracking systems, and hybrid trackers typically perform better than single-technology-based tracking.

questions.question: Why can fiducial tracking and natural feature tracking both be part of visible light tracking, yet one requires added landmarks while the other depends on existing scene features?
questions.reference_answer: Visible light tracking uses optical cameras, which are common in consumer and wearable devices, and it includes fiducial and natural feature tracking. Fiducial tracking adds artificial landmarks, called fiducials, to aid registration and tracking. Natural feature tracking uses features already present in the environment, such as points, corners, or line intersections, and uses feature descriptors to match them and estimate camera pose.

questions.question: How does 3D structure tracking support the idea of augmented reality as a state that augments the real environment?
questions.reference_answer: Augmented reality is the intermediate state where the real environment is augmented with virtual content. 3D structure tracking obtains 3D positions of points in the scene and creates 3D models of structures in the environment for augmentation of the real-world view. Kinect Fusion uses structured light depth sensor data to create such models and also tracks the pose of the Kinect.
